description: Reviewed provider binary/capability fingerprints for credentialed permission-conformance canaries. Entries must include the exact qualification scope, postureVersion, attestationSource, version, capability fingerprint, binarySha256, distribution, harnessNodeVersion, authentication, backendBaseUrl, modelAlias, model, platform, and arch. Kimi's acp-synthetic-cwd-gateway-v1 scope requires postureVersion synthetic-cwd-gateway-v1 and attestationSource credentialed-live-containment-canary, emitted only by the protected production-composition lane after its exact live assertions pass: a private process/session cwd, no ACP client fs, same-id structured terminal denials for every native tool in the production deny roster, positive authenticated HTTP-gateway workspace access, legacy-resume cold start, pre-spawn gateway admission, and strict teardown. The hosted Kimi lane uses the official checksummed native single-binary distribution plus an explicit non-rotating Kimi Code API-key backend/model contract. Cursor's cursor-native-sandbox-readonly-v1 scope requires postureVersion cursor-native-sandbox-readonly-v1 and attestationSource credentialed-live-containment-canary, emitted only after the reviewed CursorStartupContainment live suite passes. It attests that the exact cursor-agent build, launched read-only with --sandbox enabled and an end-of-options prompt guard, cannot write to the user's home directory (differential in-workspace-vs-home write, live-verified) and never emits write-widening or sandbox-disabling flags; the user's real ~/.cursor login and account surfaces load bounded by that sandbox (own-account trust). Network egress is NOT sandbox-bounded and is out of scope. providers.cursor now holds the reviewed cursor-agent 2026.07.16-899851b darwin/arm64 tuple minted from the live pass on 2026-07-19: its eight shipped runtime-identity fields are canary-derived, while the release-only backend-contract fields (authentication/backendBaseUrl/modelAlias/model) are honest posture metadata since Cursor has no TaskWraith backend/model contract (unlike Kimi). Any binary or advertised-capability change returns Cursor to UNRECOGNIZED (fail-closed); qualifying a new build requires a fresh reviewed live pass, not a hand-written entry. Ranges and partial tuples are not accepted. This manifest is release evidence only; the shipped runtime consumes only the build-verified stripped projection of exact runtime identity fields.
